## Working Papers

::: {.paper}
### Conflict Among Slope Ski Tourers in the Alps: Applications for Machine Learning
::: {.coauthors}
with Klaus Moeltner and Martin Schnitzer
:::

Applies machine learning methods to study conflict between ski tourers on shared Alpine slopes, with implications for recreation management and policy.

::: {.links}
[Under Review]{.badge .badge-wp}
:::
:::

::: {.paper}
### Environmental Stress and Labor-Market Constraints on International Migration

Examines how environmental stress interacts with labor-market conditions at origin to shape international migration flows, using bilateral panel data across 138 countries.

::: {.links}
[Under Review]{.badge .badge-wp}
:::
:::

::: {.paper}
### Warnings from the Web: Using Online Media Data to Anticipate Crop Conditions
::: {.coauthors}
with Mario Ortez, Michael Smith, and Nicole Widmar
:::

Uses natural language processing of online media to construct early-warning indicators of adverse crop conditions.

::: {.links}
[Under Review]{.badge .badge-wp}
:::
:::

::: {.paper}
### A Replicable Framework for Ex-Ante Property Value Impact Assessment of Proposed Utility-Scale Solar Facilities
::: {.coauthors}
with Zhenshan Chen
:::

Develops a replicable framework for projecting property value impacts of proposed utility-scale solar facilities before construction, combining matched comparable sites, difference-in-differences estimation, and welfare translation.

::: {.links}
[Under Review]{.badge .badge-wp}
:::
:::

::: {.paper}
### Recovering Direct Price Effects of Environmental Amenities in Housing Markets: Regression and Causal Machine Learning Model Assessment with Empirical Monte Carlo Simulation
::: {.coauthors}
with Zhenshan Chen and Klaus Moeltner
:::

Uses an empirical Monte Carlo simulation on over one million upstate New York property transactions to evaluate regression and causal machine learning methods for recovering unconfounded price effects of environmental amenities in hedonic models.

::: {.links}
[Under Review]{.badge .badge-wp}
:::
:::

::: {.paper}
### Grid Tariffs and Household Electricity Use
::: {.coauthors}
with Benjamin Kirchler, Andrea Kollmann, and Johannes Reichl
:::

Analyzes how a novel peak-based grid tariff affects household electricity consumption, using an experiment with Austrian households.

::: {.links}
[In Preparation]{.badge .badge-wp}
:::
:::

## Publications

::: {.paper}
### Farmer Participation in Payment for Ecosystem Services Programs: Evidence From Eastern North Carolina
::: {.coauthors}
with Greg Howard. *Journal of the Agricultural and Applied Economics Association*, 1–16 (2026).
:::

Uses a discrete choice experiment to estimate farmer willingness to accept voluntary Payment for Ecosystem Services contracts in North Carolina's Tar-Pamlico watershed.
